summary:
The Neosho Mucket is a freshwater mussel that once filtered the clear, flowing rivers of the Arkansas River system across Kansas, Missouri, Oklahoma, and Arkansas. A quiet inhabitant of gravel and sandy riverbeds, it spent its life anchored in current, slowly purifying the waters around it. Its range once stretched broadly across the Neosho and Verdigris basins, a subtle but essential presence in the ecosystems it called home.

Over decades, its world was transformed by dam construction, agricultural runoff, sedimentation, and mining. At least eleven major dams fragmented its habitat, isolating populations and severing the connected river corridors it needs to survive. Its range has shrunk by 70%, and it continues to decline — a quiet disappearance from waters it shaped for centuries.
